text:
samira: Heads-up — opened a small docs PR to cover HSM provisioning portability and a tiny containerized HSM-proxy example for on-prem sealed hubs. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/2991. Main asks: sanity-check the Windows ARM64 copy/paste snippets, confirm nftables vs iptables note, and fix any broken anchors I touched.

tom: Nice. Can you paste the container example and the Windows snippet here so we can eyeball flags?

samira: Sure, copying the essential bits from the PR: 

```bash
# docker-run example for an HSM proxy (illustrative)
docker run --rm \
  -v /etc/hsm/certs:/certs:ro \
  -e HSM_PIN_FILE=/run/secrets/hsm_pin \
  -p 127.0.0.1:33000:33000 \
  redwood/hsm-proxy:latest \
  --pkcs11-provider /opt/hsm/lib/pkcs11.so --listen 0.0.0.0:33000 --tls-cert /certs/proxy.pem
```

```powershell
# conn-check quick (Windows ARM64 literal copy/paste)
.\\conn-checker.exe --host 10.11.12.13 --port 33000 --timeout 6 --use-sni --ca C:\\certs\\redwood-ca.pem
```

samira: Also added a short portability note: "Some HSM provisioning scripts assume GNU sed, bash, and /usr/bin/env paths — call out BusyBox and PowerShell differences and provide sed-compatible one-liners for both."

uma: Good call. For the container example, add a security callout: mount the pin as a file from a secret store and do not bake it into images. Suggest `--secret` or a tmpfs rather than ENV for pins.

tom: On networking: please add a short bullet comparing nftables and iptables behavior for sealed networks — specifically masquerade and conntrack defaults that affect hairpin/NAT reflection. Some customers spin up HSM proxies in containers on gateways and hit hairpin issues.

samira: Added a brief nftables vs iptables note and an example nftables rule for HSM ports: 

```bash
nft add table ip rw
nft add chain ip rw input { type filter hook input priority 0; }
nft add rule ip rw input tcp dport {33000,2222} accept
```

samira: Also included a short troubleshooting checklist for HSM ops after rotation: verify NTP (<5s skew), re-import chain into appliance, check PKCS11 slot numbering (firmware can renumber), and confirm connector TLS certs are trusted by private CA bundle.

uma: One tiny nit: in prose prefer forward-slash paths but keep literal Windows escapes in code blocks (so users can copy/paste). Also add a certutil example for Windows import: `certutil -addstore -f \"ROOT\" C:\\certs\\redwood-ca.pem`.

samira: Done. I also fixed a moved anchor the linkcheck flagged (offline bundle -> /install/airgap/bundle-verify). docs-bot output was helpful.

docs-bot: Linkcheck: PR #2991 -> 1 moved anchor detected and replaced: /install/offline-bundle -> /install/airgap/bundle-verify. Label: doc:link-fix.

infra-bot: Quick infra note: when running proxy in a container on gateway, ensure host's sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 and that iptables/nftables rules don't block hairpin reflection; added a short line in the PR.

tom: LGTM from docs side. Another small suggestion: show a tiny Docker Compose snippet for teams that prefer compose over raw docker run.

samira: Pushed a follow-up commit with a minimal compose example and a security callout about not committing compose files with secrets. Also added a one-liner for verifying both offline bundle and manifest checksums: `sha256sum redwood-offline.tar.gz redwood-offline-manifest.json`.

uma: Looks good. Approving. Merge on green and consider expanding the HSM portability section into a short page next sprint.

samira: Thanks all — will merge on green and add a changelog note. (thread: PR coordination, containerized HSM-proxy example, Windows ARM conn-check snippet, nftables vs iptables notes, secret mounting guidance, and link fixes)
